title: Efficient Routes Between Every Pair
real_world_story: The organization wants to know the fastest route between every pair of devices in its network. Because the network is set up and queried frequently, engineers precompute all-pairs shortest latencies once so that any route question can be answered instantly.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Devices, network links and their latency costs
real_world_connection.query_represents: A request for the fastest route between two devices
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Precomputing the shortest route between every pair of devices

problem_statement: Given N devices numbered 0 to N-1 and E undirected network links with latency costs, precompute the shortest latency between every pair of devices using the Floyd-Warshall algorithm, then answer Q queries.
task: For each query (S, D), print the shortest latency from S to D, or -1 if D is unreachable from S.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and E. The next E lines each contain three integers u v w describing a link between devices u and v with latency cost w. The next line contains Q, the number of route queries. The following Q lines each contain two integers S and D describing a query.
output_format: Print Q lines, each containing the shortest latency for the corresponding query, or -1 if the destination is unreachable.

examples.explanation: The shortest latency from 0 to 3 is 45 via 0->1->2->3, and from 3 to 1 it is 35 via 3->2->1.

expected_algorithm.name: Floyd-Warshall
expected_algorithm.reason: Floyd-Warshall computes the shortest path between every pair of devices in O(N^3), so that all Q route queries can be answered in O(1) each.

hint: Initialize a distance matrix with direct link latencies and infinity elsewhere.
For every intermediate device k, try to improve each pair (i, j) by routing through k.
After the algorithm completes, a value of infinity means the pair is unreachable.
real_world_takeaway: Floyd-Warshall lets an organization precompute the fastest route between every pair of devices, so repeated route queries can be answered instantly.
